title: Physics-informed hybrid machine learning for predicting impact resistance of carbonate natural building stones (PHy-CPP): code and data
description:
Reproducible code and dataset for the paper "Physics-informed hybrid machine learning for predicting impact resistance of carbonate natural building stones" (Özkan, Sarıışık & Kundak, 2026).

The PHy-CPP model augments an Extra Trees regressor with two physics-informed compensatory channels — one driven by Impact Strength (IS) and one by Fe2O3 content — blended through dual sigmoid functions, to predict the impact resistance (BS EN 14158) of carbonate dimension stones from rebound hardness, Knoop hardness, plate thickness, and a SHAP-weighted compressive index.

Metrics are reported under nested, leakage-controlled Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation (17 folds, n = 51). Headline dual-channel performance: R² = 0.9623, MAPE = 7.83%, MAE = 0.717 kPa, RMSE = 0.993 kPa; bootstrap mean R² = 0.9615, 95% CI [0.948, 0.972]. The pipeline is fully deterministic (SEED = 42, N_EST = 500) under the pinned environment in requirements.txt (Python 3.12, scikit-learn 1.6.1).
notes: Associated research article: Construction and Building Materials. Raw experimental measurements were originally reported by Sarıışık et al. (2016/2017); please cite that source for the underlying experimental campaign.
